newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown--training plan will create real jobs.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown--training plan will create real jobs.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said he was confident that the training opportunities for young people which his "welfare-to-work" programme will create would lead to real jobs.
In an interview with BBC television, he said that although the "windfall tax" on privatised utilities would be a one-off levy, it would finance the programme for five years.
"We are not creating a programme that will last for six months and then run out of money. We have costed it over a five-year parliament and that I think is the right thing to do," Brown said.

He was speaking before a breakfast meeting with executives from 50 companies at which he planned to explain the three billion pound welfare-to-work programme which will form the centrepiece of his first budget on July 2.
Under the programme, employers will receive 60 pounds a week for six months for each unemployed person under the age of 25 to whom they give work.
The finance minister said unemployment had been neglected for too long and he aimed to use the potential of young people in the economy and prevent the emergence of an underclass.
Asked if the training opportunities for 250,000 young people would turn into real jobs, he replied: "I think they will...These are good opportunities, I hope with high-class employers."
Brown said there were skill shortages in many sectors of industry throughout Britain.

"We are putting money into this programme -- three billion pounds of government money -- so that we can break this vicious cycle of poverty, unemployment, lack of skills and therefore unemployability. The companies I have talked to are anxious to help."
